summary: A fast, loud party game where players draw cards hoping not to pull an exploding kitten, using a hand of joke and defusal cards to manipulate the deck and dump bad luck on opponents. It plays in a few minutes per round with lots of shouting and bluffing rather than deep strategy.
praised: Simple rules anyone can pick up in a minute
Great with large groups and non-gamers
criticised: Very little actual decision-making once you're used to it
Luck of the draw can decide the game regardless of play
Party Pack adds volume/variants but not real depth
Wears thin with dedicated hobbyist groups

interaction.kind: take that and push your luck
interaction.detail: Players directly target each other with attack, skip, and 'make another player draw' cards, and the shared deck is the entire game state everyone is manipulating. Almost every turn is a decision about who to hurt or how to dodge the exploding kitten, so the game is nearly all interaction with no private tableau.

scoring.how_you_win: Players take turns drawing from the deck, using action cards to skip, peek, or force others to draw; whoever draws an Exploding Kitten is eliminated unless they play a Defuse, and the last player left un-exploded wins outright — there is no point score.
